extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical mechanics / mathematical physics (readers of Newton's Principia)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and states classical-mechanics propositions about attraction (gravitation) of spheres, rings, solids, and related constructions, including methods to compute resultant forces and to infer local force laws from measured totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXX (Theorema XL): Total attraction of a sphere ∝ area ANB
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaeram alicujus ... particulas singulas aequales tendant aequales vires centripetae ... dico quod vis tota, qua corpusculum P trahitur versus sphaeram, est ut area ANB comprehensa sub axe sphaerae A B (linea curva A N B quam punctum N perpetuo tangit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: divide axis and sphere into corresponding equal elements (Dd laminae sphaericae); each lamina's force on P ∝ DE·Ff (or to element measure) and sum of laminae forces is proportional to sum of corresponding areas DN·nd, hence to area ANB. Use decomposition into annuli/laminae; corollaries replace DN by expressions determined by particular distance-laws of elementary forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries to Prop. LXXX: variants for different particle-law dependences
rubrics_metrics.description: Corol. 1–4: If particular centripetal force to each particle is (a) constant in all distances, (b) reciprocal to distance, (c) reciprocal to cube of distance, or (d) more generally reciprocal to any power V, then the total force by the sphere on P is still proportional to the same area ANB with DN chosen accordingly (substitute DN := DE × PS / ? etc as in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each corollary gives the required substitution for DN (the ordinate applied) as a function of given distance-dependence of the pointwise force; the summed area method of Prop. LXXX then yields the total attraction. The text shows explicit algebraic substitutions and resulting proportionalities for common power-laws (constant, 1/r, 1/r^3, and general powers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXI (Problema XLI): Construction to measure area ANB
rubrics_metrics.description: Stantibus jam positis, mensuranda est area A N B. Construction: from P draw tangent PH to sphere at H and normal HI to axis, bisect PI in L; then using relations (PE^2 = PS^2 − SE^2 + PSD etc.) one obtains an ordinate DN expressed in three parts whose application along AB produces areas (rectangular and hyperbolic parts) whose combination yields the desired area ANB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a geometric-construction algorithm and several worked examples for different pointwise force laws: (Ex.1) forces ∝ 1/distance, (Ex.2) ∝ 1/distance^3 (or cube), (Ex.3) quadruplicate decay, etc. The method reduces the problem to describing areas by parabolic/hyperbolic/rectangular contributions, erecting perpendiculars and asymptotes, and subtracting parts to obtain ANB. The text gives explicit algebraic expressions for the three parts of DN and their mapped areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXII: Relation of interior vs exterior attraction via subduplicate ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: In sphaera centro S intervallo S A descripta, si capiantur S I, S A, S P continue proportionales: dico quod corpusculi intra sphaeram, in loco quovis I, attractio est ad attractionem ipsius extra sphaeram in loco P, in ratione composita ex subduplicata ratione distantiarum a centro (S I, S P) & subduplicata ratione virium centripetarum in locis illis P & I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives general rule: when radii (SI, SA, SP) are in continued proportion, attraction at an interior point relates to that at an exterior point by composing subduplicate (i.e., square-root) ratios of distances and of local pointwise force strengths. Examples illustrate inversion: for particle forces ∝ 1/r, ∝ 1/r^2, ∝ 1/r^3, etc., yielding specific simplified ratios (equality, SP/SA, SP^2/SA^2, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXIII (Problema XLII): Attraction of a spherical segment on the center
rubrics_metrics.description: Invenire vim qua corpusculum in centro sphaerae locatum ad ejus segmentum quodcunque attrahitur. If the spherical surface has physical depth O, and elementary particle forces are reciprocal to a power with index n, then the total attracting force by the segment RBSD on the center P is proportional (per prop. LXXIX) to DE^q × O ... and is represented by the curvilinear area B D I obtained by applying ordinate FN along DB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives recipe: replace the physical spherical surface by its effective lamina (depth O) and compute the proportional content (DE^q × O with appropriate powers). The resulting force is represented geometrically by a curvilinear area produced by applying an ordinate proportional to that content along the segment's base DB. Uses prior proposition LXXIX for lamina contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXIV (Problema XLIII): Attraction of a segment on an external axial point
rubrics_metrics.description: Invenire vim qua corpusculum extra centrum sphaerae in axe segmenti cujusvis locatum, attrahitur ab eodem segmento. The attraction of the whole segment on a point P on its axis equals the sum of attractions of its two subdivided parts (compute prior using Prop. LXXXI and LXXXIII).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes splitting the segment into two parts at the appropriate spherical section; compute the attraction of each part using the propositions for interior/central and exterior points and add them. The proposition points to application of LXXXI (for external part) and LXXXIII (for internal part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXV: Contact vs separated attraction when particle forces decay faster than inverse-square
rubrics_metrics.description: Si vires particularum trahentis, in recessu corporis attracti, decrescunt in ratione plusquam duplicata distantiarum a particularibus, attractio longe fortior erit in contactu, quam cum vel minimo intervallo separantur ab invicem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: if elementary forces drop faster than inverse-square, then a shell or body contributes little except near contact; hence adding or removing remote parts changes attraction negligibly whereas contact regions produce significant excess attraction. Applies equally to concavo-convex spheroidal bodies and their cavities; removing or adding material far from contact can arbitrarily change shape without much changing remote-attraction, so contact effects dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXVI: Very fast-decaying particle forces give arbitrarily large contact attraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Si particulae ex quibus corpus attractivum componitur, vires in recessu corporis attracti decrescunt in triplicata vel plusquam triplicata ratione distantiarum a particularibus: attractio longe fortior erit in contactu, quam cum attrahens & attractum intervallo vel minimo separantur ab invicem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By solutions exhibited in Problem XLI (examples 2 and 3), attraction in near contact can grow without bound for sufficiently steep decay rates of elementary forces. This extends to concavo-convex bodies and is used to argue general results about arbitrary shaped attracting bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXVII: Scaling of accelerative attractions between similar bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora duo sibi invicem similia, & ex materia aequaliter attractiva constantia, seorsim attrahant corpuscula sibi ipsis proportionalia & ad se similiter posita: attractiones acceleratrices corpusculorum in corpora tota erunt ut attractiones acceleratrices corpusculorum in eorum particulas totis proportionales, & in totis similiter positas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bodies are similar and made of the same attracting material, decomposing into proportional particles shows that accelerative attractions of whole bodies scale as the attractions between corresponding particles and as the totals of their parts. Corollaries give explicit scaling for various pointwise force-dependences (e.g., if elemental forces ∝ 1/r^2 then accelerations scale with bodies' cubic sizes and inverse-square of separation; other power-laws yield different scalings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXVIII: If particle forces ∝ distance, resultant tends to center of gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: St particularum aequalium corporis vires attractivae sint ut distantiae locorum a particulis: vis corporis totius tendet ad ipsius centrum gravitatis; & eadem erit cum vi globi ex materia consimili & aequali constantis, & centrum habentis in ejus centro gravitatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by pairwise resolution: forces from equal particles can be resolved into components about the common center of gravity G and mutual components cancel, so the resultant acts as if the entire attracting mass were concentrated at G. The result extends by induction to all particles: the total force is the same as that of a globe centered at the center of gravity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXXXIX: General many-particle extension to common center of gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora plura ex particulis aequalibus constantia, quarum vires sunt ut distantiae locorum a singulis: vis ex omnium viribus composita tendet ad trahentium commune centrum gravitatis; & eadem erit, ac si trahenta illa, servato gravitatis centro, coirent & in globum formarentur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same argument as prior proposition generalized: decompose bodies into equal particles; resultant of all pairwise contributions directs to common CG and equals attraction of a composite globe placed at that common CG. Corollary: the motion of attracted body will be like motion toward a spherical body concentrated at CG (elliptical/ellipsoidal motions as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XC: Attraction of a circular ring on an axial point ∝ area AHIKL
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad singula circuli puncta tendant vires aequales centripetae, crescentes vel decrescentes in quacunque distantiarum ratione: inventa est vis qua corpusculum quodvis P in recta (perpendiculare ad circulum) attrahitur; dico quod attractio est ut area AHIL ducta in altitudinem AP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: take at each ring point E a local ordinate FK proportional to the pointwise force; then the annulus' contribution is proportional to the rectangle under radial AE and latitude Ee (or to PExFf). Summing all annuli around the circle gives total attraction ∝ the area AHIKL (the curve traced by FK). Corollaries: for FK ∝ 1/(distance^2) the attraction reduces to inverse-square behavior (explicit expression), and in limit of infinite radius/density the plane result with specified power-law exponents follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XCI: Attraction of a solid of revolution on its axis ∝ area LABL
rubrics_metrics.description: Invenire attractionem corpusculi in axe solidi rotundi cuius puncta singula tendunt vires aequales centripetae in quacunque distantiarum ratione decrescentes. The attraction of the solid on point P in its axis is as the area LABL (the curve LKI described by tangency of K) integrated along the axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: cut the solid by planes perpendicular to axis into circular sections; for each section use Prop. XC to represent its contribution by a local ordinate FK; the locus of tangency of these FK curves forms LKI whose area LABL (when taken in AP direction) gives the total attraction. Corollaries give explicit formulae for cylinders and spheroids (e.g., cylinder attraction formula and spheroid relations comparing attraction with that of a sphere of given semidiameter). Also gives treatment of interior points (attraction ∝ distance from center when inside certain spheroids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XCII: Determining the local decrement law of centripetal forces from measured attraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Dato corpore attractivo, invenire rationem decrementi virium centripetarum in ejus puncta singula tendentium. Construct a regular sphere or cylinder with a figure whose law of attraction matches a chosen decrement law (per Props. LXXX, LXXXI, XCI); then perform experiments to measure attraction at various distances. From the measured total-attraction law deduce the decrement law of elementary forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical method: choose a regular reference body whose theoretical relation between interior pointwise law and total attraction is known (per earlier propositions). Measure the actual attraction of the given body at different distances, compare with the reference mapping, and invert the relation to obtain the exponent or functional form describing how elemental forces decline with distance within the actual body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio XCIII (Theorema XLVII): Decay of attraction of a solid with a plane face
rubrics_metrics.description: Si solidum ex una parte planum, ex reliquis autem partibus infinitim, constet ex particulis aequalibus aequaliter attractivis, quartem vires in recessu a solido decrescunt in ratione potestatis cujuslibet distantiarum plusquam quadraticce, & vi solidi totius corpusculum ad utramvis plani partem constitutum trahatur: dico quod vis illa attractiva, in recessu ab ejus superficie plana, decrescet in ratione potestatis, cujus latus est distantia corpusculi a plano, & index ternario minor quam index potestatis distantiarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case analysis: (1) For the point outside the solid, decompose the solid into parallel planar slices; each planar slice's contribution ∝ CH^{-n} etc; summing gives the body's attraction ∝ distance^{-m} with exponent m smaller (ternario minor) than the pointwise exponent n. (2) For point inside near the plane, symmetry cancels many contributions; the net attraction follows analogous reciprocal-power with exponent related to slice-sum behavior. Corollaries: if the solid has two infinite parallel bounding planes, the attraction of the finite portion can be found by subtracting infinite parts; if the particle exponent is triplicate the simple assertion fails (because distant parts can dominate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium: Procedure to derive motion under given attraction laws (series/ordinate method)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is attracted perpendicularly toward a given plane by a specified law, its motion can be found by solving (per Prop. XXXIX) the motion of rectilinear descent and composing with uniform parallel motion; one resolves applied ordinates in convergent series. Examples: when ordinatim applied length is parabolic and parameters m=2, n=1 then the motion is a parabola; if hyperbolic ordinates with m=... the motion is a hyperbola, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives operational recipe: represent the attraction field by an ordinate applied along a base and expand the ordinate in an infinite series of infinitesimal parts, treat the force proportional to that series term-by-term, and sum to obtain the required force-law and resulting trajectory. The scholium gives algebraic manipulations (terms involving m and n, with limits) and concrete examples showing which combinations of exponents yield parabolic or hyperbolic trajectories.
